subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in headless browser for reliable web access without external dependencies

question: Should OpenClaw make browser-rendered access a first-class `web_fetch`/`web_search` capability, or keep the managed browser as a separate explicit tool?
rationale: Current main intentionally separates HTTP/provider web tools from the security-sensitive browser tool; merging them changes product behavior, session handling, proxy policy, and browser trust boundaries.

options.title: Design browser-backed web access
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical product/security tracker and require an approved design before implementation.

options.title: Keep browser separate
options.body: Define `web_fetch` and `web_search` as non-rendering provider tools and route JS or login pages only through the explicit browser tool and docs.

options.title: Split into narrower work
options.body: Move each approved slice to narrower issues such as rendered extraction benchmarks, proxy/isolation, sandbox endpoints, and cookie persistence before closing this umbrella.

recommendation.title: Design browser-backed web access
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical product/security tracker and require an approved design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin boundary, current web-tool split, and recent browser security policy history point most strongly to this owner for product-direction routing.
